summary: Asks IANA to mark BGP path attribute values 30, 31, 129, 241, 242 and 243 as Deprecated.

eli5.summary: Some numbered slots reserved for BGP were never properly used. This marks them as retired.

subtitle: Marking unused BGP attribute values as deprecated.

tldr.problem: BGP implementations had been using attribute values 30, 31, 129, 241, 242, and 243 without official IANA assignment, squatting on slots that new protocols needed.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8093 asks IANA to mark these values as Deprecated in the BGP Path Attributes registry so they can no longer be used for new standards.
tldr.outcome: These squatted values are officially retired, and the attribute slots can be managed more carefully in the future.

today: RFC 8093 is a Proposed Standard. The specified BGP Path Attribute values are permanently marked Deprecated in IANA's BGP Parameters registry.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
BGP, the routing protocol that runs the Internet, uses numbered attributes to carry routing information. However, certain attribute values had been used in deployed BGP implementations without being officially assigned by IANA. This became a problem when RFC 8092 tried to assign value 30 for the BGP Large Communities attribute and discovered that a widely deployed BGP-4 implementation already used that value for something else, breaking early adopters of Large Communities.

Investigation confirmed that values 30, 31, 129, 241, 242, and 243 had all been squatted by various vendors or implementations. RFC 8093 asks IANA to officially mark these values as Deprecated.
sections.eli5: Some routers were using numbered slots without permission. When someone tried to use slot 30 officially, it broke things. This RFC marks all the sneakily used slots as retired.

sections.title: Registry Update
sections.content: IANA has marked BGP Path Attribute values 30, 31, 129, 241, 242, and 243 as Deprecated in the BGP Path Attributes registry. The Deprecated marking means that use is not recommended. These values are no longer available for new standards or specifications.
sections.eli5: IANA put a big X on those six numbered slots to show they're no longer for sale.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 8093 is a Proposed Standard. The deprecated values remain locked to prevent further collisions, and new BGP extensions should use available unassigned values.
sections.eli5: This is the official decision to lock up those six parking spots forever.
